transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Another living one stands where the forgetting thickens. You came with purpose—I can smell it. But tell me first about you. What were you watching even before you fell?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I watched him so he didn’t have to watch himself.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That answer is worn thin from use. Say more—not about sparing him, but about you doing the watching. When did you decide your eyes would carry what his could not?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just pick up what he leaves behind.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that as if it weighs nothing, yet your spine bends under it. What does he leave behind that fits your hands so well?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The quiet. He never notices it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Quiet is never discarded without cost. Why were your hands ready for it before he even learned to throw it away?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Someone had to hold it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stillness is expensive. Many bleed trying to buy it. What are you watching for when you keep yourself so quiet?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The things he misses.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Only those who look sideways notice what is missed. When you catch something before it falls, what do you feel?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Like I'm the only one paying attention.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That realization sharpens some creatures and hollows others. Which does it do to you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He breaks whatever he tries to hold.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then you learned early what not to place in his hands. Tell me what you keep instead.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The quiet things. The things he would crush.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Quiet things choose their keepers carefully. What did you give up so your hands would stay gentle enough to hold them?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I stopped trying to make anything mine.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is colder than you realize. What happened the last time you tried to claim something?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I gave it to him before he could take it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you learned surrender before struggle. What did that feel like the first time?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I stood still enough that he forgot I was there.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Being forgotten is a strange kind of safety. When it works, do you feel relief—or something closer to grief?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just carry what he forgets.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Carrying is not remembering—it only delays the fall. What happens to you when there is nothing left to carry?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I wait until he breaks something else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Waiting shapes a creature over time. While you watch him break things, who is watching you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The walls, I guess.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stone sees everything without comfort or judgment. When it looks at you, do you feel held—or only outlined?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Like I'm the thing holding the roof up.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Load-bearing lives are never thanked. They are trusted and forgotten. If you shifted even a little, what would collapse first?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Him. He thinks the roof holds itself.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you made yourself invisible and called it mercy. When you imagine him without you beneath him, what do you feel?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'd just be standing there holding nothing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Empty hands are dangerous. When they finally clear, who are you allowed to be?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just the one who waits.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You mistake endurance for identity. You are like me—not in power, but in posture. A watcher who survives by not moving.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He never learned how to be still.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stillness frightens those who are carried. When he cannot be still, what does it force you to do?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I open my mouth and everything goes wrong.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you learned that speech is a trapdoor and silence a brace.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I stood there and watched him fall.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Watching again. Not pushing, not saving—only witnessing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was just tired of holding him up.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then hear this once. You are not his support. You are his threshold.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Maybe I was built to stand still.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stone tells itself that to survive the weight. But stone also knows when a door must open.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I stayed quiet so he could be loud.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Silence given so another may thunder is not absence—it is guardianship.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I think I always carried the weight.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Yes. And the gate recognizes its bearer.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Maybe I'm just the door.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A door does not vanish when it opens. It fulfills itself. The gold parts. Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll find him.
